stories.title: Islamabad deal collapses; US strikes Iran again and reimposes the blockade
stories.summary: The memorandum broke down over who controlled shipping: Iran attacked tankers using a southern route near Omani waters. The US struck back from Jun 26, rescinded its oil licence and launched extensive airstrikes on Jul 7. Trump declared the deal 'over' on Jul 8 and reimposed the blockade from Jul 14. An Iranian strike killed three US troops in Jordan on Jul 17.

causes.why: Vague clauses on control of the strait
Rival claims to control the strait

stories.unplaced: Strikes and sea attacks across the Gulf; no single site.

stories.title: NATO's Ankara summit pledges €70bn for Ukraine
stories.summary: At the Ankara summit, allies reaffirmed Article 5, backed the target of 5% of GDP for defence by 2035, and pledged €70 billion for Ukraine in 2026 with at least as much in 2027. Trump said Ukraine would get a licence to produce Patriot interceptors.

causes.why: Alliance patched up after the Greenland crisis
Madrid named Russia the main threat; Ankara funds that judgment

stories.title: Houthis declare a naval blockade on Saudi shipping
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthis declared a maritime embargo on Saudi vessels in the Bab el-Mandeb. CRS says they resumed attacks on Saudi Arabia and Saudi-linked shipping in July, after airstrikes attributed to Riyadh diverted a flight from Iran carrying Houthi personnel. That ended the cross-border calm that had held since the 2022 truce.

causes.why: Renewed US–Iran war widened the Houthi front
The 2022 truce never became a settlement

stories.unplaced: Declared over the Bab el-Mandeb, which has no coordinates in the place list.

stories.title: Chinese coast guard fires water cannon at Philippine ships at Scarborough
stories.summary: Chinese coast guard vessels fired water cannon at Philippine fisheries and coast guard ships near Scarborough Shoal on Jul 23–24, with one ship coming within about seven metres. China said it drove away vessels operating illegally in its waters.

causes.why: China tightening control of the shoal

stories.title: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey sign the Mecca mutual-defence pact
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, under which an attack on one is an attack on all.

causes.why: Houthi threat to Saudi shipping
Pakistan's rising value to Gulf and US partners

analysis.text: Riyadh is hedging against an unreliable US umbrella by buying Sunni military depth, with Pakistan's nuclear status in the background.

stories.unplaced: The sources do not name the signing venue.

stories.title: Ukraine's drone campaign drives Russian diesel exports to multi-year lows
stories.summary: The IEA said Ukrainian drone strikes cut Russian refinery runs to about 3.8 million barrels a day, a 20-year low, and diesel output by about 30%. Bloomberg reported diesel and gasoil exports fell to 80,000 barrels a day in early August. Moscow imposed its first diesel export ban in July and was set to extend curbs through October.

causes.why: Ukraine's answer to Russia's long war on its grid

analysis.text: Kyiv's refinery strikes plus Hormuz created the diesel shortage that later made Russian diesel a bargaining chip for Washington.

stories.unplaced: Strikes on many refineries across Russia; no single site.

stories.title: US–Iran memorandum expires with no final deal
stories.summary: The 60-day window for a final US–Iran deal closed on Aug 17. Diplomacy stalled. Two days later Trump announced an 'Economic D-Day' sanctions drive, and Israeli forces stayed in southern Lebanon (about 5% of Lebanese territory, per CRS).

causes.why: Deal already broken in July

stories.title: Syria's Kurdish-led SDF merges into the army and dissolves; US delists Syria
stories.summary: SDF leader Mazloum Abdi said integration with Damascus was complete on Aug 20, and the SDF formally dissolved on Aug 25, after a January government offensive took much of its territory. On Aug 24 the US removed Syria from its state sponsors of terrorism list and delisted HTS.

analysis.text: Damascus is consolidating with Washington's blessing, closing a front Turkey cared about and opening Syria to Gulf investment.

stories.unplaced: A political merger; no single site.

stories.title: Houthis seize Mokha and tighten their grip on Bab el-Mandeb
stories.summary: During a September ground offensive the Houthis took the Red Sea port of Mokha and coastal areas next to the Bab el-Mandeb, and The National reported they seized a key island in the strait. CRS says they closed the strait to Saudi-linked shipping. The National reported traffic through the strait halved, to about 15 crossings a day from 30.

causes.why: Escalation from naval blockade to ground offensive

stories.unplaced: Mokha has no coordinates in the place list yet.

stories.title: Drones from Iraq hit Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline; flows halted
stories.summary: Drones launched from Iraq struck sections of the East-West pipeline, which carries crude to Yanbu on the Red Sea, in the Riyadh and Medina areas. Saudi Arabia shut it as a precaution. Saudi Arabia attributed the attack to Iraq-based groups and held off retaliating; Iraq dismissed a security commander and ordered an investigation.

causes.why: Renewed war widened attacks on Gulf energy

analysis.text: Hitting the Hormuz bypass shows Iran's network can threaten both Gulf exits at once.

stories.unplaced: Sources name only the Riyadh and Medina areas, not exact sites.

stories.title: Warsh's Fed raises rates for the first time in three years
stories.summary: The Fed raised its target range by a quarter point to 3.75%–4.00%, its first hike in three years, defying Trump. Warsh said price stability remained the priority.

causes.why: New chair
Oil shock kept inflation hot

stories.title: Trump signs the Russia and Iran sanctions act
stories.summary: Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act. It authorised tariffs of up to 500% on Russian goods and up to 100% on the top five buyers of Russian crude or gas, due to take effect Oct 18. The Kremlin said new sanctions would make a peace deal harder.

causes.why: Escalates the sanctions regime begun in 2022

stories.unplaced: A bill signing; no event site.

stories.title: US, Denmark and Greenland agree an expanded US military presence
stories.summary: The three governments agreed to expand the permanent US military presence in Greenland while recognising Danish sovereignty and Greenlandic self-determination. The text, signed Sep 22, gives the US new defence areas and bars non-NATO states from persistent bases.

causes.why: Davos 'framework' turned into a treaty

stories.title: Zelenskyy tells Trump at the UN that Ukraine is ready for an energy ceasefire
stories.summary: Meeting Trump at the UN General Assembly, Zelenskyy said Ukraine supported a full halt to strikes on energy infrastructure, including refineries, if Russia did the same.

causes.why: Refinery strikes were Kyiv's bargaining chip

stories.unplaced: Meeting at the UN in New York; no place entity yet.

stories.title: Tigray's leaders declare a 'defensive war' as TPLF forces attack
stories.summary: Tigray's regional government said it had entered a defensive war after reported federal drone and artillery strikes. TPLF forces took Tigray's main airports and attacked federal positions in Afar and Amhara as part of a seven-group alliance against Abiy Ahmed. Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights to three Tigray airports.

causes.why: January clashes were the prelude

analysis.text: Eritrea is widely believed to back the TPLF, which Asmara denies. That turns an Ethiopian civil war into an Ethiopia–Eritrea contest over Red Sea access.

stories.unplaced: Attacks across Tigray, Afar and Amhara; no single site.

stories.title: Soybeans, planes and rare earths: the US–China truce looks fragile
stories.summary: CNBC reported that China's farm purchases under the May truce were uneven and that the deal's rare-earth and aircraft pieces remained fragile ahead of the Nov 10 expiry of China's suspension of its rare-earth controls.

causes.why: Implementation of the May deals

stories.title: Trump rejects Iran's seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran offered to reopen the strait within seven days if the US ended its blockade, released frozen assets and waived oil sanctions. Trump said the offer 'would not be acceptable' and that Iran wanted a deal because it was 'losing so badly'. CRS had reported in mid-September that the two sides were again trading limited strikes amid a redoubled US sanctions campaign.

causes.why: No deal after the window closed

stories.title: Last US troops leave Iraq
stories.summary: The US completed its withdrawal from Iraq, pulling its last troops from an air base in the Erbil area. Iran-backed militias celebrated, and Kurdish officials warned of a security vacuum.

causes.why: Iran-aligned blocs have run Iraq's government since 2022
Attacks from Iraqi soil raised the cost of staying

analysis.text: Iran's allies get Iraq to themselves. The open question is whether the militias stand down or turn on the Kurds and the Gulf.

storylines.name: Levant: Lebanon, Gaza & Syria after the wars
Gulf realignment: Saudi–UAE split & the Mecca pact
